title: Normalized proxy that reshapes OpenAI ChatCompletions requests & streaming deltas
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a normalized proxy layer that accepts OpenAI Chat Completions API v1 requests and maps them to Redwood's internal ChatRequest shape and back for responses and streaming. Goals: preserve semantics for function/tool calling, structured output markers, streaming deltas, multipath choices, and stop-token behavior while avoiding breaking internal runtime optimizations (batching, KV reuse, quantization-friendly execution).
acceptance_criteria: Proxy accepts standard OpenAI ChatCompletions payloads (messages, functions, top_p, temperature, n, stop, stream) and returns responses compatible with OpenAI expectations
Streaming path emits delta events that mirror OpenAI's event shapes (role/content fragments, function_call with name/arguments deltas) and sets final "[DONE]" marker appropriately

Function/tool calling: mapping must support both explicit function call requests and model-initiated function_call objects; final calls must be returned in response or via a structured finish_reason per OpenAI convention
Compatibility tests cover: multiple choices (n>1), stop token edge cases, echo=true, message-level name/role differences, and non-UTF8-safe argument fragments
Performance regression <5% p50 latency change on synthetic CC workload when proxy enabled with typical batching (seq=512)
technical_decisions: Translate OpenAI 'messages' -> internal 'message' with canonicalized roles: 'system','user','assistant','tool'
Stream chunk canonicalization: emit 'delta' events that include only changed fields to minimize size and match OpenAI's incremental CRDT-like behavior

Function calling: buffer 'arguments' fragments on stream using an explicit 'function_call.arguments_fragment' key and stitch on the client/console side; final 'function_call' object included as a top-level field on completion event

Stop token handling: implement a pre-filter stage that recognizes OpenAI-style stop sequences and converts them to runtime early-termination cues rather than truncating tokens post-render, to preserve streaming deltas
n (choices): when n>1, allocate a stable per-choice stream id and interleave events in deterministic order; final 'choice' objects will include 'index' and 'finish_reason'
Backpressure and chunk coalescing: the proxy will expose a max_chunk_bytes setting and coalesce small deltas to reduce websocket overhead without violating token ordering semantics
design_notes: UX expectation: Redwood Console streaming inspector must reconstruct argument fragments into a single 'arguments' field for display and evals
